King David. Arguably the most revered figure in the Hebrew Bible and Jewish tradition, a shepherd who became Israel's greatest king.

Anointed king by the prophet Samuel while still a boy, David became an instant hero by defeating the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and stone. Samuel chose him over his older brothers, fulfilling a divine choice based on his heart rather than his appearance. For years David lived as a fugitive, pursued by the jealous King Saul, yet he remained loyal and refused to kill Saul even when he had the opportunity.

David brought the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem and established it as the religious and political center of Israel. He conquered surrounding nations and expanded Israel's territory to its greatest extent, making it a regional power. But his relationship with Bathsheba brought grave sin into his reign: their adultery resulted in the death of her husband Uriah.

He fathered Solomon, who would succeed him and build the First Temple, fulfilling David's desire to construct a permanent home for God's presence. His life spans the books of First and Second Samuel and is recorded in First Kings. Through his reign, he established Jerusalem as Israel's capital and set the spiritual and political foundation for later Jewish hope and identity.
